donnees.titre: Five-Year Real-World Outcomes of iStent inject W® Combined with Phacoemulsification in Ocular Hypertension and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
donnees.resume: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the long-term real-world efficacy, safety, and functional and structural outcomes in patients with ocular hypertension (OHT) or primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) undergoing trabecular micro-bypass surgery with the iStent inject W®. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 149 eyes of 149 patients with OHT or POAG who underwent implantation of the iStent inject W®, combined with phacoemulsification, and were followed for up to five years. Outcomes included intraocular pressure (IOP), number of hypotensive medications, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural parameters, and visual field indices. Follow-up data were available at 1 year (n = 123), 2 years (n = 94), 3 years (n = 61), 4 years (n = 35), and 5 years (n = 15). Results: BCVA improved significantly after surgery (p < 0.01). A mild but statistically significant decline in visual field index (VFI) was observed over time (p = 0.03), consistent with expected long-term glaucoma progression. OCT structural parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. IOP was significantly reduced at all postoperative visits except at years 3 and 5, where reductions did not reach statistical significance despite a sustained downward trend. Medication burden was significantly reduced at all time points (p < 0.01). Men exhibited lower postoperative IOP than women (p = 0.02), and OHT patients had higher IOP levels than those with POAG (p < 0.01). Conclusions: In a real-world clinical setting, the iStent inject W® provided sustained IOP reduction, durable medication burden reduction and long-term structural stability over five years. These findings support its long-term clinical effectiveness in the management of OHT and POAG.
